_about: Historical baseline causal analysis, not current conformance results. Categories: a = native concept or mapping absent; b = deliberate difference (only a shared-spec-approved deviation can earn conformance); c = bridge conformance bug. Actual runner replies/events decide PASS. The final-six merits review applies the original hash-pinned v0 normative rules, not a new profile.

T01.why: Upload and seal are not job events and do not advance a revision (revision stays 3 at the upload step). After finish the bridge reports revoked:false (authority_revoked is set by cancel only; a finished job is fenced by its terminal status). The result and artifacts otherwise match.
friction: artifact id: art_ prefix required; owner sees a global id, worker a client id
claim activity: lease_ms is server config, not a claim argument

T02.note: Passes. The bridge dedups submit on (request_id, payload hash), returns duplicate:true and writes no event. Equivalence holds without a key store.

T03.note: Passes only through the adapter error map: 'request_id conflict' is mapped to KEY_CONFLICT. The bridge has no key, so it cannot tell KEY_CONFLICT from EXISTS (see T04).

T04.why: No per-command idempotency key. A different key with identical content on the same job returns success (duplicate:true), not EXISTS.

T05.why: No revision compare-and-swap. The second claimant loses with 'already claimed' (BUSY), not REVISION. Safety holds: exactly one winner in 24 parallel races, both winners observed (V01).

T06.why: Strict run fails only on leaseUntil (60000 vs 100): lease length is server configuration (minimum 60 s), not a claim argument. With the lease-scaled diagnostic clock it passes: a second principal cannot use the first worker's claim ('invalid claim' mapped to STALE_EPOCH).
friction: scoped revocation errors: 'invalid claim' covers wrong worker, stale epoch and unknown claim

T07.why: A worker mutation at the lease deadline succeeds. The bridge treats expiry as takeover eligibility, not revocation (store.assertClaim checks the active claim row only). Authority ends when the drain sweep (every 500 ms in production, skipped while paused or during a usage break, lease clock restarts at process start) or a takeover claim commits.
friction: claim activity: any tool call naming the claim refreshes the lease

T08.why: Strict run fails only on leaseUntil. Lease-scaled run passes: scheduler sweep requeues, a second worker takes epoch 2, and the old claim's finish is fenced.

T09.why: No renew operation, renewed event, renewal receipt or revision. The only lease refresh is an idempotent re-claim by the same claimant (adapter maps renew to it). Replay re-applies the refresh instead of returning a cached receipt, and it survives restart.

T10.why: Same claimant can refresh an expired but unswept lease (idempotent re-claim touches activity before the expiry check). The profile requires LEASE_EXPIRED.

T11.why: Strict run fails only on leaseUntil. Lease-scaled run passes: a scheduler tick one unit before the deadline leaves the lease in place.

T12.why: No revision field on worker commands. A stale-revision progress is accepted and appended.

T13.why: No question or answer records, no answered/consumed events. Semantics that exist: the owner note is durable across SIGKILL and the worker reads it with get after restart.

T14.why: No question records. An owner note with no open question is accepted.

T15.why: Strict run fails only on leaseUntil. Lease-scaled run passes: a worker cannot post an owner note because the bridge owner surface needs a per-request capability (invalid owner capability mapped to FORBIDDEN).

T16.why: No one-answer rule. A second owner note on the same topic is appended and accepted.

T17.why: QUESTION: progress notes are not question records. finish(completed) succeeds with an unanswered QUESTION note open. (The bridge forwards the question to the owner but does not gate completion on it.)

T18.why: Strict run fails only on leaseUntil. Lease-scaled run passes: progress after cancel is TERMINAL.

T19.why: Owner notes are not tied to a live attempt or open question. A note on a cancelled job is accepted (inert: the worker cannot act on a terminal job). Candidate minor bug if the bridge wants notes refused on terminal jobs.

T20.why: Owner notes are job-scoped context. A note posted after takeover is delivered to the new epoch (claim and get return owner_notes). The profile forbids mapping a late answer to a new attempt.

T21.why: Finish after cancel is refused with assignment_cancelled (TERMINAL); the output is kept only as bounded late_evidence and no report exists. What still differs is the revision counter, because upload and seal write no event.

T22.why: Cancel after finish is correctly TERMINAL and the receipt survives. Only difference: get reports revoked:false for a finished job.

T23.why: Only journal granularity differs (no uploaded/sealed events or revisions). Behavior matches: after restart, finish with an unsealed artifact is rejected (UNSEALED).

T24.why: Only journal granularity differs. A sealed artifact survives restart and finish works without re-upload.

T25.why: Only journal granularity differs. A wrong digest is rejected (DIGEST). The bridge verifies the digest only; seal has no size argument.

T26.why: Shared v0 R6 requires the current epoch to stage/seal its own reference. Legacy sealed inheritance is not an approved v0 exception. Native v5 rejects predecessor references in protocol finishes, preserves immutable origins and permits explicit restage/reseal under a new reference; non-protocol inheritance stays unchanged.

T27.why: finish does not re-bind source or policy. A result whose source differs from the job source is accepted.

T28.why: Passes except one field. Duplicate finish after restart returns the original receipt with no new event. get reports revoked:false for a finished job where the profile expects true.

T29.why: Strict run fails only on leaseUntil. Lease-scaled run passes: a conflicting finish is rejected ('contradictory report' mapped to KEY_CONFLICT).

T30.why: Owner wait is a live HTTP long-poll. There is no waiter registration, waiter_registered event or revision. A late wait on a terminal job returns the terminal result immediately.
friction: durable inbox/waiters dying on restart (partly addressed by dot-worker inbox)

T31.why: No waiter registry. The long-poll dies on restart (adapter aborts it). The durable inbox (owner-states) still shows the finished result after SIGKILL; that is the recovery path.
friction: durable inbox/waiters dying on restart (partly addressed by dot-worker inbox)

T32.why: No predicate-specific waiters. The adapter must remember predicates itself; the bridge inbox has one flag set per request.
friction: durable inbox/waiters dying on restart (partly addressed by dot-worker inbox)

T33.why: dispatch and delivery_result are UNSUPPORTED: the drain loop sends notifications itself; no externally claimable outbox item.

T34.why: dispatch and reconcile are UNSUPPORTED. The bridge has internal uncertain-delivery recovery (recoverSends, reconcileRequest) but no externally supplied evidence path.

T35.why: dispatch, delivery_result and reconcile are UNSUPPORTED.

T36.why: Inbox is per request, not per waiter. It is durable across restart and ack suppresses it. Ack writes a native consumed journal event (owner read marker), which the profile does not expect. Retrying ack returns marked:false (not replay-safe) per V07.
friction: durable inbox/waiters dying on restart (partly addressed by dot-worker inbox)

T37.why: No waiter expiry. The unread inbox entry stays regardless of the waiter's expiresAt.

T38.why: No retention horizon, no tombstones. get returns the job after the retainUntil time; a re-submit with other content is a request_id conflict, not TOMBSTONE.

T39.why: observe_stop is UNSUPPORTED (stop evidence exists only for bridge-run sandbox checks). Cancel itself returns stop:unverified and survives restart.

T40.why: Strict run fails only on leaseUntil. Lease-scaled run passes: a blocked finish succeeds with an unanswered question.

T41.why: Only journal granularity differs. Bytes are immutable after seal (second upload EXISTS).

T42.why: dispatch is UNSUPPORTED, so the closed-schema INVALID on an injected destination cannot be exercised. The bridge fixes the destination at submit (delivery=none or t3:thread).
